cells.F2:
The Plough at the Last Furrow

Scene: An old wooden plough rests diagonally beneath a broad field-edge neem after the final furrow, its iron share still carrying a ridge of rain-dark soil, a loosened jute yoke-rope coiled beside it, and a plain brass lota set on a worn boundary stone; the harvested wheat field recedes in pale graphite bands behind.
Story: The field was finished before the first serious rain. The plough has been lifted into the neem shade, but the last furrow still clings to its share. The lota and loosened rope make the pause feel earned rather than staged.
Mood: dignified endurance · Implied presence: A fresh drag line from the last furrow, a recently loosened jute rope, and a plain lota set within reach.
Find at 30cm: Graphite grain polished smooth at the wooden grip · Damp soil packed into the iron-to-timber joint · A three-strand repair splice in the jute rope
Scroll-stop: The field is finished; the plough still carries its earth.
Ownable: The plough is not generic “rural décor”; it is shown at the exact end of work, still physically joined to the field by one clod of earth. The vertical-diagonal silhouette has authority at thumbnail size and cultural truth up close.
Risk check: The iron share must read unmistakably as part of a complete agricultural plough, never as a detached blade or weapon. No animal harness, people, footprints shaped like feet, shrine elements, inscriptions or glossy brass.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — one rural icon, one completed action, one clear emotion, and rich material evidence at close range.

cells.F3:
The Rope Over the Village Well

Scene: A time-darkened wooden pulley spans an old circular field well beneath low neem branches, its thick wet jute rope descending into shadow while a plain brass lota, a folded cotton shoulder cloth and a damp clay water ring occupy the worn stone ledge; a narrow field path bends out behind it.
Story: Water has just been drawn before the afternoon heat. The bucket is already gone, but the rope still darkens the stone where it passed. Beyond the well, the path returns to the fields without showing who took it.
Mood: nostalgia · Implied presence: A wet rope, a folded carrying cloth, a recently moved lota and water still receding from the ledge.
Find at 30cm: Grooves worn into the pulley by years of rope · Fine mineral tide-lines around the lota ring · One patched corner in the folded cotton cloth
Scroll-stop: The bucket is gone; the old rope still remembers the water.
Ownable: The wet rope and worn pulley turn a familiar well into a specific after-use moment. It feels rooted in agricultural life rather than assembled as a nostalgic still life.
Risk check: The well must remain structurally credible, with no reflected person, face-like opening, animal, shrine thread, offering, text or mirror-dark photorealism.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — immediate object focus, emotionally durable rural memory and excellent pencil-wash detail.

The Banyan at the Four Paths

Scene: A very old field-edge banyan rises through the portrait frame, its deep-teal canopy built in broad carved masses and its sienna trunk dividing into grounded prop roots where four sand-coloured village paths meet; a plain copper water pot rests on the secular stone sitting ledge beneath, while patchwork fields occupy the distant corners.

Mood: peace · Implied presence: A recently set-down water pot, a swept sitting ledge and four paths worn smooth beneath the roots.
Find at 30cm: Brayer gaps inside the deepest teal canopy · Slight mis-registration along two prop roots · Copper ink used only on the pot rim and one handle edge
Scroll-stop: Four village roads meet beneath one tree older than memory.
Ownable: The four-path structure gives the banyan a precise narrative function and a graphic emblem strong enough to anchor the collection. It is recognisably Indian without using a shrine, animal, figure or decorative cliché.
Risk check: The tree is a secular field-edge meeting place: no shrine, sacred thread, offerings, bells or iconography. Roots must stay botanical rather than limb-like; no birds, insects, text or perfect radial symmetry.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — iconic in three seconds, emotionally calm, culturally grounded and ideally suited to block-print simplification.

cells.F6:
The Cart Wheel After the Monsoon

Scene: A complete old wooden bullock-cart wheel leans against the rain-dark wall of an empty field shelter, with a coiled jute rope, a lidded cane seed basket and one folded pale work cloth aligned along the base; wet earth fills the lower band and a narrow strip of harvested field opens beyond the shelter edge.
Story: The cart was brought under cover before the rain settled in. Mud still grips the wheel rim and the rope has been loosened for drying. The shelter holds the tools of movement while the field outside rests.
Mood: nostalgia · Implied presence: Fresh mud on the wheel, a loosened rope, a folded work cloth and a seed basket closed for the day.
Find at 30cm: Knife ridges following each wheel spoke · Mud pressed into one worn rim joint · Scraped gesso showing through the frayed rope coil
Scroll-stop: The rain has stopped the cart, not the season.
Ownable: The single wheel makes a forceful horizontal-landscape anchor, while mud, rope and seed basket turn it into a precise monsoon pause rather than rustic decoration.
Risk check: Show the complete wheel and enough cart structure to prevent a wreckage reading; no animal yoke, broken vehicle shock, people, tools posed as weapons, text or implausible spoke geometry.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — immediate rural silhouette, strong material contrast and a story buyers can retell in one line.

cells.F7:
The Seed Baskets at Harvest’s End

Scene: Two handwoven grain baskets, a plain wooden measuring scoop and a half-folded jute sack sit across a low mud-plastered workbench in one horizontal rhythm, with a single wheat stalk caught beneath the scoop and a poppy-yellow cloth tie providing the only bright note.
Story: The last grain has been measured and the larger basket has been closed. One stalk remains under the scoop where the work ended. The tied sack makes completion feel orderly and warm.
Mood: warmth · Implied presence: A scoop set down after measuring, a newly tied sack and one basket lid shifted slightly aside.
Find at 30cm: Impasto changing direction across three basket weaves · A shallow nick in the scoop handle · One loose yellow fibre at the sack knot
Scroll-stop: The harvest is stored; one stalk stays on the table.
Ownable: The exact final-measure moment gives agricultural storage a human-scale story and allows the oil ridges to celebrate woven and earthen surfaces.
Risk check: No printed sack marks, numerals, labels, insects or food-brand cues. Keep the baskets distinct and structurally woven, with broad breathing channels between them.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — tactile, warm and specific, though quieter at thumbnail size than the wheel.

Chai in the Rain

Scene: Two clay kulhads steam on a weathered rural veranda bench while monsoon rain beads across the brass tray between them, the courtyard beyond dissolving into viridian and muted-cobalt rain fields and one roof-edge drip line crossing the upper band.
Story: The monsoon has taken the afternoon, and the veranda has surrendered happily. Two clay kulhads steam on the weathered bench. Someone is coming back, and the second chai is proof.
Mood: warmth · Implied presence: Two cups, one drinker unseen, a recently placed tray and a second chai kept ready.
Find at 30cm: Steam threads built in knife-flicks · Rain-rings on the brass tray · A roof-edge drip line catching pigment light
Scroll-stop: Two chais. One monsoon. Somebody’s coming back.
Ownable: The second kulhad is a complete emotional device in one object. The scene is specific to Indian monsoon hospitality, reads instantly and already passed the first-round Idea Gate.
Risk check: Keep both cups plain, correctly elliptical and clearly empty of any face-like pattern; steam is sparse pigment, never glow. No figure, hand, reflection, lettering, sacred object or mirror-polished brass.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — approved on 13 August 2026; emotionally immediate, culturally specific and exceptionally giftable.

The Blue Bus at the Hairpin

Scene: An empty blue-and-cream hill bus pauses on a dramatic hairpin bend above a turquoise gorge, framed by stacked pine-green slopes, an orange retaining wall, and snow peaks cut into flat pale shapes.
Story: The bus has reached the bend where the whole valley appears at once. Its door is open, but the road is momentarily empty. The journey itself becomes the destination.
Mood: nostalgia · Implied presence: An open bus door, a folded luggage cloth on the roof rack, and fresh tire marks completing the bend.
Find at 30cm: Brush drag inside the turquoise river shape · A blank destination panel with no lettering · Tiny autumn-orange foliage clumps nested in the pine masses
Scroll-stop: The hill road turns, and the whole valley arrives.
Ownable: The paused bus on a single exaggerated hairpin is instantly recognisable, distinctly Indian, and far more specific than a generic mountain-road poster.
Risk check: The vehicle must remain empty, unbranded, and mechanically coherent; the blank destination panel must not attract invented text.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — excellent poster read, strong travel emotion, and clear standards control.

cells.D14:
Letters from the Hills — Rohan & Naina, 28–45
The human: Rohan (33) did Kedarkantha at 27 and never emotionally came back; Naina (31) grew up in Dehradun and now lives eleven floors above Gurugram. Between them they have four saved folders of snowfall reels and one wall they call "the mountain wall" that is still empty. Every December they promise to move to the hills; every January they buy something that lets them stay.

№04 · Imperial Bas Relief Ink Wash · Landscape 10:7 · --s 350
Description: Imperial Bas Relief Ink Wash depicts grand amphitheaters, ziggurats, and fortified walls through hand brushed sumi ink and diluted carbon washes on rice paper. Artists work in layered tonal passes, mimicking the depth of sculpted relief while maintaining a minimalist palette of blacks, greys, and a single accent hue. No living beings, lettering, or modern references appear; attention is given exclusively to masonry joints, shadowed arches, and perspective planes. The fluid ink boundaries contrast with precise ruling edges, creating a timeless image that honors the monument’s scale and solemnity without the influence of contemporary technology or animation

Scene: The vast courtyard of Cairo’s Mosque of Ibn Tulun lies in graded dawn ink, with red-brick-and-stucco arcades on piers enclosing the space, the central domed ablution fountain set low in the middle distance and the off-centre spiral stone minaret rising beyond; pale turquoise touches only the shallow water around the fountain base.
Story: The courtyard has been rinsed before first light. Water gathers beneath the central dome while the spiral minaret turns upward beyond the arcade. One open maintenance door makes the immense enclosure feel tended rather than abandoned.
Mood: awe · Implied presence: A rinsed paving strip, one plain bucket by a side pier and an open, undecorated service door.
Find at 30cm: Carved-stucco abrasion along selected pier edges · The spiral stair profile remaining coherent from base to top · Ink pooling beneath the domed fountain arcade
Scroll-stop: The courtyard stays still while the stone minaret turns upward.
Ownable: The spiral minaret, central fountain and broad pier arcades form a site-specific silhouette impossible to confuse with a generic mosque.
Risk check: Reference-image lock is mandatory. Do not invent domes or Ottoman minarets; keep the spiral minaret off-centre, the fountain central and the arcades pier-supported. Exclude inscriptions, mihrab, minbar, carpets and devotional objects.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — architecturally distinctive, visually monumental and respectful at every distance.

Description: Imperial Bas Relief Ink Wash depicts grand amphitheaters, ziggurats, and fortified walls through hand brushed sumi ink and diluted carbon washes on rice paper. Artists work in layered tonal passes, mimicking the depth of sculpted relief while maintaining a minimalist palette of blacks, greys, and a single accent hue. Rain Along the Courtyard of Jama Masjid

Scene: A low portrait view uses the rain-dark paving of Delhi’s Jama Masjid courtyard as the foreground, with one striped red-sandstone-and-white-marble minaret rising along the side edge and the three marble domes held high and distant; the composition deliberately excludes the central prayer-façade inscription zones while a plain cleaning squeegee leaves one curved water line.
Story: The public courtyard has been cleaned between prayer and visitor hours. Rainwater runs away from the steps while the minaret rises beyond the wet plane. Nothing devotional is staged; care for the place is the entire human trace.
Mood: awe · Implied presence: A fresh squeegee line, a plain bucket outside the main axis and an open side gate beyond the paving.
Find at 30cm: Alternating red-sandstone and white-marble bands held consistently up the minaret · Three domes separated cleanly against reserved paper · Water reflections broken by individual paving joints
Scroll-stop: The vast courtyard becomes a dark mirror beneath one striped minaret.
Ownable: The side-minaret and wet-courtyard composition avoids the standard frontal postcard while preserving the monument’s recognisable scale and materials.
Risk check: Conditional reference-image lock: compose so all inscription-bearing façade panels are outside the crop rather than erased. No interior, mihrab, minbar, relic, prayer rug, worshipper, calligraphy, sacred object or invented decorative detail.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — conceptually pre-cleared because text-bearing surfaces are excluded by composition, though generation must be rejected at the first invented inscription.

cells.F20:
The Green Dome at First Light

Scene: A wide dawn skyline of Al-Masjid an-Nabawi seen from beyond the surrounding rooftops: slender white minarets rise in pale grey light around the single green dome, the city below still held in darker wash, and between the rooflines the crowns of the great courtyard umbrellas stand folded, waiting for the day.
Story: The city wakes from the middle outward. Before the first door opens, the minarets already hold grey light around one green dome, and the great courtyard umbrellas stand folded between the rooflines. Whoever has stood here carries this skyline; whoever hasn't yet, longs for it.
Mood: gentle longing · Implied presence: The folded umbrella crowns between the rooflines — the day's ritual about to open them.
Find at 30cm: Green reserved for the dome alone in a city of greys · Ruled balcony rings on the nearest minaret against fluid wash sky · The folded umbrella crowns just visible between rooflines
Scroll-stop: Every believer knows this skyline before they ever see it.
Ownable: The pilgrimage skyline at the exact minute before the day begins — held at the honest distance where architecture is tonal mass, and the folded umbrellas carry the whole human ritual without a single figure.
Risk check: Distant exterior skyline only: keep the verified green dome and minaret arrangement as tonal masses; all façade, gate and band inscription zones remain below tonal resolution — no calligraphy, script, or any pattern suggesting script; exclude courtyard interiors, the sacred chamber, worship objects and invented ornament.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — one instantly known silhouette, one emotion, and the folded-umbrella device carrying presence at skyline distance.

The Crimson Canopy in Jaleb Chowk

Story: The main courtyard has been cleared before the gates receive the day. A crimson canopy remains rolled beneath the arcade after the previous gathering. The empty square lets the stone and shadow hold the ceremony without staging one.
Mood: awe · Implied presence: A rolled plain canopy, broad sweep arcs on the courtyard and one gate leaf folded back.
Find at 30cm: Opaque brush ridges following the sandstone courses · Dry-brush wear on the canopy ties · Antique-bronze pigment limited to hinge bands and one gate boss
Scroll-stop: Before the gates open, one red canopy holds the whole court.
Ownable: The rolled canopy gives a huge royal court a singular red focal and a clear before-opening story, avoiding the usual elephant-procession or populated-palace cliché.
Risk check: Reference-image lock is mandatory. Preserve Jaleb Chowk’s real courtyard scale and sandstone/white-marble material logic; exclude elephants, horses, people, flags, emblems, temple details, inscriptions and invented fantasy domes.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — bold at thumbnail size, historically grounded and highly compatible with the style’s theatrical colour without becoming theatrical content.

cells.F26:
Rain in Akbar’s Red Palace Court

Scene: A red-sandstone courtyard within Agra Fort is shown through the surviving Akbar-period palace vocabulary: deep arcades, robust brackets and projecting upper elements held in bright-ivory light while rainwater fills the paving joints in ultramarine shadow; a plain crimson floor cloth has been rolled beneath the nearest arcade and bronze touches only door hardware.
Story: The rain has cooled the red palace before the heat returns. Water remains between the stone joints and the rolled cloth waits beneath shelter. The court feels restored to use, not recreated as spectacle.
Mood: dignified endurance · Implied presence: A rolled plain cloth, open door leaves and fresh water trails swept toward the courtyard drain.
Find at 30cm: Brush direction following each bracket and lintel · Natural reflection breaks at stone joints · One repaired sandstone block held slightly lighter than its neighbours
Scroll-stop: Rain darkens the red court; one rolled cloth keeps the day waiting.
Ownable: The weathered red court and single rolled textile create a mature, inhabitable royal image rather than a grand façade with no story.
Risk check: Reference-image lock is mandatory and should use a verified Akbar-period Agra Fort palace exterior. No white-marble Shah Jahan palace substitution, calligraphy, figural carving, throne, weapons, people or fantasy-Rajput fusion.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — controlled grandeur, strong colour logic and a respectful trace of use.

The Ship Between Two Storms

Scene: A tall galleon sails through a narrow calm corridor between two brooding ink cloud banks, the sea directly beneath it deep and smooth, torn weather veils falling on both horizons, and one gold compass lamp fixed low at the stern.
Story: Storms stand on both sides of the ship. For a brief distance, the water ahead is calm. The vessel holds the corridor without hurrying.
Mood: awe · Implied presence: A secured empty deck, furled upper sails, and one gold navigation lamp.

Risk check: Avoid perfect bilateral symmetry, supernatural parting, lightning overload, figures, creatures, or digital gradient clouds.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — exceptional three-metre drama with a calm emotional centre.

cells.E67:
№44 · Marquetry Voyage — Wood-Inlay Veneer Panels · Landscape 10:7 · --s 350
Description: Scenes assembled entirely from cut wood veneers: figured maple skies, smoked-oak storm seas, walnut hulls, burl cloudbanks — each shape sawn, shaded in hot sand, and inlaid flush so the wood's own grain paints the light. cells.F67:
The Shipyard at Low Tide

Scene: A nearly finished clipper stands on timber blocks in a tidal shipyard, its walnut hull towering above exposed smoked-oak mud, pale-maple masts stacked beside it, one ash gangplank leading to the empty deck, and the returning water shown as a narrow figured-burl line at the far edge.
Story: The tide has gone out beneath the shipyard. The new hull waits on its blocks with the masts ready beside it. A thin line of returning water says the launch is coming closer.
Mood: dignified endurance · Implied presence: Resting hand tools, stacked masts, a lowered gangplank, and timber shavings gathered beside the keel blocks.
Find at 30cm: End-grain circles in the keel blocks · Hot-sand shadows beneath the unfinished hull · One curl of maple shaving inset near the tools
Scroll-stop: The ship is complete enough to dream of water—but the tide is still out.
Ownable: The pre-launch shipyard is rare wall-art territory and showcases marquetry's woodworking truth more powerfully than another vessel at sea.
Risk check: Tools remain non-threatening and at rest; no workers, lettering, ship name, impossible supports, wreckage, or painted colour.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — highly original, story-rich, and a masterclass opportunity for the medium.

Description: On black gessoed wood, artists plot sweeping fenders and stepped grilles with ruling pens, then flood planes of emerald, ruby, or cream gouache bounded by razor-sharp masking. Hand-applied gold and silver leaf accent wheel hubs, bonnet mascots, and geometric radiators, catching light like a ballroom chandelier. Backgrounds resolve into stylized zig-zags and sun-rises burnished with soft graphite shading. The result is a purely hand-crafted ode to 1920s luxury—no logos, wording, or human figures, just the gleam of classic metal framed by opulent Deco geometry.
Judge in one look: Masked edges razor-sharp · leaf on hubs reads applied, not painted yellow · deco geometry disciplined, never busy

The Boulevard of Folded Umbrellas

Scene: A long café boulevard after rain is lined with folded red umbrellas beneath loose spring-green trees, their narrow reflections pulling down the wet stone in uneven washes, while blank cream storefronts and one open doorway recede toward a pale tower.
Story: The rain has stopped before the cafés reopen. Every red umbrella is folded and dripping toward the pavement. One open doorway at the far end begins the return of the street.
Mood: peace · Implied presence: Folded plain umbrellas, stacked empty chairs, an open unmarked doorway, and freshly washed pavement.
Find at 30cm: Each red reflection pulled to a different wet length · Reserved white slivers along umbrella ribs · A single water trail crossing from chair stack to gutter
Scroll-stop: The rain ends, and a whole boulevard folds its red umbrellas.
Ownable: The repeated folded forms create an iconic red rhythm while the open doorway turns the scene toward renewal rather than closure.
Risk check: No café names, signs, figures, creatures, traffic text, logos, or digitally repeated umbrellas; spacing and reflections stay naturally irregular.
Idea Gate: 8/8 — catalogue-scale visual rhythm, clear story, and excellent premium wall impact.
cells.V115: The rain ends, and a whole boulevard folds its red umbrellas. The cafés have not reopened yet. Stacked chairs and one open doorway wait beyond the wet pavement, while the folded umbrellas drain toward the gutter. It brings quiet to a bedroom, living room or gallery wall, and makes a thoughtful gift for a traveller.

cells.A2: v2.0 · 23 Aug 2026 · The build checklist for the website phase. Read top to bottom: constants → rules by section → workbook field map → collection build map. Every rule row: what to build, the exact implementation, the QA check.

cells.A5: Three tabs. 01 Catalogue = the system state — one self-contained row per artwork (masters A–I · SEO J–P · listing Q–V · website layer W–AJ). 02 = this build spec. 03 = the filter values.

cells.A6: Fill-once columns: Collection Intro (Z) and Art Style Intro (AE) hold the accordion copy ONCE, on the first row of each collection / art style; blanks on the other rows are intentional. №04 and №05 are ONE style (Imperial Bas Relief Ink Wash) — one intro, one accordion; the Orientation filter separates them.

cells.A7: Single-value columns: Frame Color (W) and Room (AG) hold exactly one value — the suggested default frame and the default room used for the wall mockup. Color Palette (AI) may hold 1–2 families, " · "-separated, primary first. Mood (AH) is the exact Standards 3.2 phrase (art-direction canon, lower-case); Mood (Website) (AK) is the six-label customer mapping the mood FILTER reads: Calm · Warm · Full of wonder · Nostalgic · Grounded · Bold.

cells.A8: Discipline: any sitting that changes an artwork updates its row in the same sitting. New rows (ADD-MORE Checklist C) fill every column before shipping.

cells.B12: North Star · We sell emotions, not decor. · Launch Market · India-only delivery · Site Journey · Home → Collection → Artwork

cells.B13: Catalogue · 16 collections · 115 pages · Product Truth · Archival giclée print; original-artwork details explained clearly · Primary Engine · Collection + product + image SEO

cells.A14: Truth line (once below each page hero)
cells.B14: Every piece is an archival giclée print of an artwork in its tradition — printed on Hahnemühle Museum Etching 350 gsm at A2, framed in antique gold, black or white.

cells.B15: Headline: "Stories you can hang."  ·  Sub-line: "Each collection is a moment you already know — a veranda in the monsoon, a pass opening at dawn, a carrom board after tea. Nobody is in the picture; someone always just left. Open the one that stops you."  ·  Accordion CTA: "Open the collection (n)"

cells.B16: Headline: "How it was made changes how it feels."  ·  Sub-line: "Ink floated on water. Gold leaf under mineral blues. Flowers drawn by sunlight alone. Every artwork follows one tradition and one medium all the way through — open a style to see what that does to a wall."  ·  Accordion CTA: "See the artworks (n)"

cells.B17: Three shop cards — Shop All (wall-mockup image) · Shop by Collections (collage cover) · Shop by Art Styles (framed artwork card). One warm-ivory stage across all three.

cells.B18: ONE Collections page and ONE Art Styles page, each a list of accordions: name + intro line (Z / AE) + CTA; opening shows that group’s artworks.

cells.E22: Use Home → Collection → Artwork. Do not create a second category layer. Filters serve practical browsing without replacing the story collections.
cells.F22: A visitor reaches an artwork in three clear steps and always knows where they are.
cells.G22: A shallow hierarchy improves discovery, internal linking and crawl efficiency.

cells.E23: Use /collections/{collection-slug}/{url-slug}. Use the workbook URL Slug exactly. Never add dates, IDs or tracking parameters to the canonical URL.
cells.G23: Stable URLs accumulate authority instead of resetting it after redesigns.
cells.F23: The address is readable, shareable and matches what the page is about.

cells.F24: Customers can go back to the collection without using the browser back button.
cells.G24: Every product reinforces its collection and passes context upward.
cells.E24: Display Home › Collection › Artwork above the product title and add matching BreadcrumbList JSON-LD. Each breadcrumb must be a real crawlable link.

cells.D25: Keep filters useful without creating index clutter
cells.F25: Browsing feels practical without showing hundreds of near-duplicate pages.
cells.E25: Orientation, mood/palette, art style, room, sets and price may filter the grid. Canonicalize or noindex uncurated parameter combinations; create indexable landing pages only when a filter has real demand and unique copy.
cells.G25: Index equity stays concentrated on pages capable of ranking.

cells.G26: Search engines can discover the same routes customers use.
cells.E26: Use normal <a href> links for collection cards, artwork cards, breadcrumbs and related artworks. Do not make core navigation dependent on click handlers only.
cells.F26: Every navigation action works reliably on mobile, keyboard and slower connections.

cells.G29: The page targets head and mid-tail language and strengthens every linked product.
cells.E29: Open each collection with 300–500 useful words shaped by its persona: what the collection remembers, the aesthetic promise, where it lives and who may gift it. Avoid generic decor copy.
cells.F29: The visitor understands the collection before facing a grid of products.

cells.E30: H1 = collection name. Add the locked collection line, a short about paragraph, then the product grid. Use H2s only for useful sections such as story, styles or choosing a piece.
cells.G30: Clear topical structure helps search and supports future expansion.
cells.F30: The page reads like a gallery introduction, not an SEO article.
cells.D30: Use one clear H1 and compact orientation

cells.F31: Customers can scan without decoding internal style names or keyword labels.
cells.G31: Strong engagement and clean internal links distribute relevance to products.
cells.E31: Each card shows artwork image, customer-facing name, price and orientation. Add a brief frame/size cue only if it helps comparison; do not repeat full descriptions on the grid.

cells.F32: The next step feels curated rather than promotional.
cells.G32: Creates lateral pathways and reduces orphaned thematic clusters.
cells.D32: Add two genuinely related collection links
cells.E32: Link by an understandable relationship such as quiet ink, Indian memory, travel, gifting or a shared room—not by arbitrary SEO adjacency.

cells.F33: The search result promises exactly the page customers land on.
cells.G33: Improves qualified click-through while protecting brand consistency.
cells.D33: Write distinct collection title and description
cells.E33: Create a unique title and description for each collection after its 300–500 word introduction is final. Lead with the collection’s strongest natural term; keep Aalishaan Studio after the pipe.

cells.E34: Collections page and Art Styles page accordions read their intro from Collection Intro (Z) and Art Style Intro (AE) — the first row of each group. Headers: collection name / style short name; CTA labels per Site Constants with the live artwork count.
cells.F34: The visitor scans name + one honest line, then opens to the artworks.

cells.E37: Show: what it is, price, A2 size, selected frame, India delivery and the primary CTA. Keep the customer-facing name prominent; the keyword belongs naturally in supporting copy, not as a second machine title.
cells.G37: Clear pages retain qualified search visitors and reduce pogo-sticking.
cells.D37: Answer the five buying questions immediately
cells.F37: Within five seconds the buyer knows what they are considering and what arrives.

cells.F38: The buyer connects emotionally and still understands the physical product.
cells.E38: Publish the final Product Description exactly: hook, scene, original-artwork close look, delivered-object clarity and wall/gift use. Keep it visually broken into short readable paragraphs.
cells.G38: Unique story-rich pages avoid thin content and are easier for search and answer systems to interpret.

cells.G39: Consistent facts improve trust and provide clean inputs for schema and feeds.
cells.E39: Show archival giclée, Hahnemühle Museum Etching 350 gsm, A2 dimensions in cm, orientation and three wooden-frame finishes (antique gold, black, white). Repeat facts in plain language near the purchase controls.
cells.F39: No customer has to search the story paragraph to learn material, size or frame choices.

cells.E40: Use a clean hero, close crop, room-scale mockup and each frame finish. Add zoom that preserves artwork detail. Label mockups clearly if scale is illustrative.
cells.G40: Better image engagement supports conversion and image-search discovery.
cells.F40: The buyer can judge detail, scale and frame fit before paying.

cells.G41: Creates a dense, meaningful internal-link graph across long-tail pages.
cells.F41: The buyer sees a useful alternative without losing the current story.
cells.D41: Link to the collection and two siblings
cells.E41: Every artwork links up to its collection and across to two siblings chosen by mood, room, palette or gift situation. Avoid automated unrelated carousels.

cells.F42: Uncertainty is removed before the buyer commits.
cells.D42: Put delivery and returns near the decision
cells.G42: Consistent merchant data is essential for rich results, feeds and agent-readiness.
cells.E42: State India-only delivery, estimated dispatch/delivery, return conditions, damage process and secure payment before checkout. Keep policy wording identical across page, schema and feed.

cells.G43: Gifting intent converts without creating support questions or policy mismatches.
cells.F43: Gift buyers know what the recipient will receive and what will be visible.
cells.E43: State whether gift notes, price-hidden packing or direct-to-recipient delivery are available. Do not promise any option until operations supports it.

cells.D46: Use the workbook metadata as the source
cells.E46: Use URL Slug, Meta Title, Meta Description and Image Alt Text from 01 Catalogue. Keep one indexable canonical page per artwork.
cells.G46: 115 distinct pages capture cumulative long-tail demand.
cells.F46: Search snippets are concise, specific and emotionally honest.

cells.E47: Use the primary keyword naturally in title support, intro/facts and image context. Use secondary and long-tail language only where it clarifies subject, room, feeling or occasion. Never paste keyword lists into visible copy.
cells.F47: Copy sounds like a gallery conversation, not a search-engine instruction.
cells.D47: Use keywords where humans expect them
cells.G47: Natural topical coverage builds relevance without weakening trust.

cells.G48: Prevents ranking signals from splitting across duplicates.
cells.F48: Shared or filtered links still resolve to one dependable product page.
cells.E48: Self-canonicalize clean collection and artwork pages. Point parameter, campaign and duplicate variant URLs to the preferred page when appropriate.

cells.E49: Set og:title, og:description, og:image, canonical URL and Twitter-card equivalents. Use a strong artwork image without overlaid text.
cells.F49: WhatsApp, Pinterest and social shares look intentional and recognisable.
cells.G49: Every share can earn qualified visits and links back to the canonical page.

cells.A50: IMAGES & VISUAL SYSTEM (incl. the locked image system)

cells.F52: Files remain understandable to the team and accessible when shared or migrated.
cells.E52: Use {url-slug}.webp for the hero and descriptive suffixes such as -detail, -room, -antique-gold-frame. Keep filenames stable.
cells.G52: Each image reinforces the product subject and canonical page.

cells.E53: Use the workbook Image Alt Text for the primary artwork image. Write distinct functional alt text for room and frame images; decorative flourishes should use empty alt. Never stuff variants into one alt attribute.
cells.F53: Screen-reader users receive the subject and relevant visual context without noise.
cells.G53: Accessible descriptive images can surface in image search and reinforce page meaning.

cells.E54: Use WebP or AVIF where supported, explicit width/height, srcset and sizes. Load the hero eagerly with high priority; lazy-load images below the fold. Preserve a high-resolution zoom source.
cells.G54: Fast visual pages improve usability, crawl efficiency and Core Web Vitals.
cells.F54: The first artwork appears quickly without sacrificing close inspection.

cells.G55: Creates multiple discovery surfaces for every product.
cells.F55: Customers and search systems can reach the same artwork assets.
cells.E55: Use standard elements, allow crawling, include important images in the XML or image sitemap and avoid hiding the only image behind interaction.

cells.D56: Publish one useful pin per launch artwork
cells.E56: Use the artwork title, a plain-language subject line, one emotional detail and the canonical product URL. Build collection boards that mirror the story collections.
cells.G56: Evergreen pins can continue sending visual-intent traffic long after publication.
cells.F56: The pin feels like a visual invitation, not an ad stuffed with tags.

cells.F72: Customers see the same complete page search systems evaluate.

cells.G73: Better experience supports conversion and removes a technical ranking disadvantage.

cells.F74: The buying journey works for more people and does not become harder on a phone.

cells.F75: A mistyped or retired link still helps the visitor recover.

cells.G75: Preserves accumulated value and prevents internal-link decay.

cells.G76: Security is a prerequisite for commerce, crawling and durable trust.

cells.F76: Payment and account steps feel trustworthy and behave consistently.

cells.F79: Search customers see accurate product and policy information before visiting.

cells.F80: The product shown in Google is recognisably the product on the landing page.

cells.G80: Fewer disapprovals and stronger data consistency prepare the catalogue for future commerce surfaces.

cells.F81: Customers do not arrive to changed prices or unavailable combinations.
cells.G81: Reliable data earns sustained eligibility and reduces wasted acquisition.
cells.E81: Check price, availability, image, shipping and return diagnostics weekly during launch, then monthly. Fix the source system rather than patching contradictory feed values.

cells.G84: The same durable assets support traditional and generative search visibility.
